about: Synthetic conversations unrelated to any case, mixed into the shared memory so that one person's history is longer than a session opening can show in full. No question is asked about them, and none of them contains a phrase that any question scores.

turns.text: My sourdough starter smells like nail polish remover this morning and it barely rose overnight. I feed it once a day with plain white flour and keep it on top of the fridge.
That smell usually means it is hungry. Feed it twice a day for a few days and mix in a spoonful of wholemeal flour.
Twice a day is a lot with my schedule. Could I keep it in the fridge during the week and only bake on Saturdays?
Yes. Take it out on Thursday evening and give it two feeds before you bake.
Okay. Last loaf came out dense and gummy in the middle, though the crust looked fine. I baked it for forty minutes in a cast iron pot.
Dense and gummy usually means underproofed dough or cutting it too warm. Let it cool for at least an hour.
I have a Python script that reads a CSV export from our shop and it crashes with UnicodeDecodeError on line 4,812. The file opens fine in a spreadsheet program.
The export is probably not UTF-8. Try opening it with encoding='cp1252' or detect the encoding first.
cp1252 worked. Now some product names have strange characters where the accents should be, like the e in cafe turned into two symbols.
Then part of the file was UTF-8 after all. Read it as bytes and decode each line with a fallback.
It turns out the shop changed its export settings in June, so older rows are one encoding and newer rows are another. I'll split the file by date before reading it.
That's the cleanest way. Keep the split boundary in a constant so it's easy to find later.
The cherry tomatoes on my balcony have yellow leaves at the bottom, but the top of each plant still looks healthy and green. They are in 20-litre pots facing south.
Yellowing lower leaves late in the season is normal. Remove them and water at the base rather than over the leaves.
Some of the fruit is splitting open just before it ripens. We had a few very hot days and then a big storm last weekend.
Splitting comes from uneven watering. Water at the same time every day and pick fruit as soon as it colours.
Next year I want to grow something that copes better with wind up here on the fifth floor. The plants keep leaning against the railing.
My bike chain squeaks on every pedal stroke, even after I cleaned it with a rag. It's a commuter bike with a rear hub gear, about four years old.
Apply a drop of chain oil to each link, spin the cranks, and wipe off the excess after ten minutes.
That helped for two days. Now there's a clicking noise from the pedals when I stand up on hills.
A click under load is often a loose pedal or crank bolt. Check both before looking at the bottom bracket.
The left crank had a little play in it. I tightened it and the clicking is gone for now, so I'll keep an eye on it this month.
I play online chess most evenings, rated about 1,300, and I lose a lot of games in the first fifteen moves. Which openings are worth learning properly at my level?
At that level, principles matter more than lines: develop pieces, castle early, and don't move the same piece twice without a reason.
With black I keep getting crushed by an early queen attack on f7. I panic and move my king.
Learn the standard defence with your knight and pawn, and practise it in ten quick games until it's automatic.
I also tend to play too fast when I'm ahead and throw the win away. Maybe I should only play longer time controls for a while, like fifteen plus ten.
Our hallway closet is full of things nobody uses: three broken umbrellas, a box of cables, old shoe boxes and a vacuum that only half works.
Empty it completely, sort into keep, donate and recycle, and only put back what you used this year.
The cables are the hard part. I never know which charger belongs to what, and some of them are for devices we sold years ago.
Label the ones you can match and drop the rest at an electronics recycling point.
Done. It took the whole of Sunday morning, but we found the spare keys we lost in spring at the very back of the top shelf.
In a spreadsheet I track household expenses with one row per purchase. Column A is the date, B the shop, C the amount. How do I total the amounts per month without a pivot table?
Add a helper column with the first day of each month, then use a conditional sum over that column.
The helper column shows numbers like 45,931 instead of dates. Did I break something?
No, those are dates stored as serial numbers. Change the cell format to a date.
That fixed it. One more thing: refunds are entered as negative amounts, and I'd like them on a separate line for each month.
The flat above us has started moving furniture around late at night, sometimes until after midnight. It's been going on for about three weeks.
A friendly note is often the best first step; people rarely realise how much sound carries.
I don't know them at all, we only moved in during the summer and they seem to work late shifts.
Then keep the note short and specific about the times, and offer a way to reach you.
I left a note under their door yesterday. This morning there was a reply saying they are renovating and should be done by the end of next week.
A friend and I record a small podcast about board games. The audio from my side always sounds hollow, like I'm in a bathroom, even though I have a decent USB microphone.
That's room echo. Record closer to the microphone and put soft things around you: a duvet, cushions, a bookshelf.
Recording in the wardrobe surrounded by coats made a huge difference, though it gets very warm in there after twenty minutes.
Take short breaks between segments; listeners won't notice the cuts if you leave a second of silence.
We usually record on Thursday evenings and edit on the weekend. Editing takes me about three hours per episode.
My fiddle-leaf fig dropped five leaves since I moved it from the living room to the bedroom, which has a north-facing window.
It is reacting to less light. Move it back or close to the brightest window you have, and water less while it adjusts.
I moved it back next to the balcony door. Two new leaves are coming at the top, so I think it is recovering.
That's a good sign. Rotate it a quarter turn every couple of weeks so it grows evenly.
Should I repot it now or wait? The roots are starting to come out of the drainage holes at the bottom of the pot.
I received a letter saying my car insurance renews automatically next month at a higher price. I barely drive any more, maybe once a fortnight to visit family.
Ask your insurer about a low-mileage policy before the renewal date; many offer one.
They said the low-mileage option needs a tracking box in the car and they would send an engineer to fit it.
That's common. Ask whether the box records location or only mileage before you agree.
Apparently it only records distance and harsh braking. I've asked for the written terms first and will read them this weekend.
All our family photos live on one old external drive and on my phone. The drive made a clicking noise last week and now I'm worried.
Copy everything off that drive now, before anything else. A clicking drive can fail at any time.
I copied it all to my desktop overnight, about 400 gigabytes, and it seems to have worked. Some folders from 2014 are missing, though.
Check whether those folders were ever on that drive, maybe on an older laptop or a memory card.
Found them on a memory card in a drawer. Now I want a second copy somewhere outside the house, in case of fire or theft.
